newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: RUGBY UNION-Bull Allen could be on the move.
newsitem.headline: RUGBY UNION-Bull Allen could be on the move.

text.p: NEW PLYMOUTH, Oct 4 - All Black rugby prop Mark Allen's 110th game for Taranaki on Sunday could be his last, the New Zealand Press Association reported on Friday.
If Taranaki lose to Otago and miss a semifinal spot, the curtain may fall on Allen's long career with the amber-and-blacks.
Last Sunday, Allen made it public that he was considering offers to play elsewhere in New Zealand.
"I'm keeping my options open," he said today.
"I haven't decided anything yet, but to be honest, I am considering some options including Taranaki."
Although he declined to say where, candidates rumoured to be trying to attract Allen were Canterbury and North Harbour.
But another province rumoured to be making a concerted effort to lure the All Black reserve prop is second division Manawatu.
It's an attractive move for Allen and one that would almost certainly keep the door open for captaincy of the Wellington Hurricanes Super 12 outfit.
Should Allen move, the Taranaki Rugby Football Union would receive a $50,000 transfer fee.
Allen said no matter what the future held, his first priority was Sunday's match against Otago.
Allen said loyalty was a great thing, but players had to consider their own financial security.
"I'm getting on a bit, I may only have three or four years left. I have to set myself and my family up for after rugby. You have to look beyond rugby."
Allen said players would go where the money is.
"At the end of the day, it's their job. They're supporting their families. They will have to look after themselves, it's a very short-term thing," he said.
"They're going to have to go where they're best looked after."
Taranaki had to look further afield, according to Allen.
"You still have to develop players and bring them through at lower levels," he said.
"But you have to be realistic, a team like Taranaki, if they think they can just sit there and rely on home grown talent to keep them there, they're only fooling themselves."
